class.name: ECSEntityProxy
class.brief_description: Inspectable dynamic Object representing a raw ECS entity.
class.description: [ECSEntityProxy] solves the "Data Visibility" problem in ECS architecture. Since raw entities are just 64-bit integers, they cannot be seen in the Godot Inspector. The proxy acts as a dynamic bridge, allowing a raw entity's component data to be exposed as standard Godot properties. When you select an entity in the editor debug view or create a proxy in GDScript, this object queries the [EntityManager] for all components attached to the target ID and dynamically populates its property list. [b]Usage:[/b] - [b]Editor Integration:[/b] View and edit ECS values directly in the Inspector during runtime. - [b]GDScript Ease-of-Use:[/b] Access ECS data using dot-notation [code]proxy.my_value = 10[/code] instead of complex dictionary lookups. [b]Warning:[/b] The proxy is an abstraction layer. It involves significant overhead compared to raw sparse-set access. Use it sparingly for UI, tools, and one-off gameplay logic, never for high-performance systems.

method.name: set_entity
method.description: Points this proxy to a specific entity ID. The proxy will immediately refresh its property list to reflect the new target's components.

method.name: get_entity
method.description: Returns the raw 64-bit ID of the entity that this proxy currently represents.

method.name: sync_telemetry
method.description: Forces the proxy to resynchronize its internal property cache with the ECS registries. Useful if components are being modified by high-frequency C++ systems and you need to see real-time updates in a custom UI or tool.
